substantiveDifference: A closing-team-approved signing-method and document-return plan for an out-of-state seller, separating electronic signing, online notarization, physical documents, funding and property handoff. sources.claim: Texas online notary is physically in Texas; signer may be elsewhere. Online notarization uses compliant audio/video and identity procedures. Electronic notarization is distinct from remote online notarization.

sources.claim: An authorized commissioned online notary may perform remote notarization by audiovisual conference rather than physical appearance. This authority does not guarantee all closing documents/transactions use online signing.

faq.q: Can I ask about selling a Houston house without traveling to Houston?
faq.a: Yes. Tell Cash As-Is and the closing team where you will be and ask which signing and property-access arrangements they can approve for the transaction. Do not assume every document can be completed online.

faq.q: Is an electronic signature the same as remote online notarization?
faq.a: No. The Texas Secretary of State distinguishes electronic notarization from remote online notarization. A document may be electronic while still requiring physical appearance; the closing team should identify what applies to each document.

faq.q: Must the seller be in Texas for a Texas online notarization?
faq.a: The Secretary of State says the Texas online notary must be physically in Texas, while the signing party may be elsewhere. Confirm transaction acceptance, identity requirements and the actual signing arrangements with the closing team.

faq.q: Does finishing the signing mean I should immediately turn over keys?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Ask the closing team when the transaction is funded and when possession must transfer under the agreement, then follow the confirmed property-handoff instructions.
